name: bullaun

attributes.attribute: a symbolic stone with a hole found at holy wells
carried healing power for conception and pregnancy
used as a receptacle for libations and fluid offerings

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: A bullaun is a symbolic stone with a hole in it. These round stones appear at holy wells and at other sacred sites in Ireland. Writers have read them as feminine symbols, much like the yoni stones of India. People held bullauns to carry healing power. The stones helped women to conceive and to survive hard pregnancies. Some bullauns were large flat boulders with basins. The basins could be natural or man-made. Women drank water from these basins as a ritual. Bullauns also served as receptacles for libations and fluid offerings.

okr.objective: Describe the bullaun as a symbolic healing stone found at Irish holy wells.
